chapter: Touring in the bus years and Jim Crow in the South
title: Doctor's visit and the dance at Foxdale
summary: The station owner will not call police; Fields is treated at a doctor's office and later x-rayed in Tulsa.

story.theme_name: Race and segregation in the jazz life
story.community_name: Segregation on the road and the bandstand

blocks.x: So, I got up, I was bleeding and I said to the man call the police. He said no, I might call the wrong one. He said I might call the police and they might take their side. He said the first thing, do you know anything about this town? He said--
He said there's a doctor's office not too far down the street, you go down there and let a doctor see whether you're hurt bad.
He said I don't think you're hurt too bad, because it didn't knock you out, but he said the way you're bleeding, you go down there, I'm not going to call the police.
So we went in the bus; he got a rag and everything and water and put it around there and told us right where to go and we went on to the office and they checked us out.

It happened that we weren't playing far from there, we were playing a base right out from Shreveport--Foxdale I believe it is that we were playing that night and we went out there, but I didn't work that night. The doctor told me don't be circulating or it might start bleeding again.
Did you have a hole in your--
Just slightly. The skull wasn't fractured, I was lucky it wasn't. They thought it was (inaudible), but as soon as I got back to Tulsa I got x-rays and everything and they found that it was okay.
